_authoredWhy: ⛑ A TRUE DRAGON, AUTHORED 2026-09-08. Erik: 'I want some dragons in the court who can POLYMORPH TO HUMAN. ⛔ DRAGONS ARE NOT ALL POLES THAT WENT WRONG.' ⚑ AND THE BESTIARY'S OWN FIRST LAW ALREADY DREW THIS LINE: 'No person. A bestiary entry has no name of its own, no want, no story being ended. IF IT WOULD BE A TRAGEDY TO KILL, IT BELONGS IN NPCs, NOT HERE.' ⚠️ SO THERE ARE TWO KINDS AND THE CORPUS SPLITS THEM CLEANLY: ⛔ A `great_manifestation` — the Ashen Wyrm, the Bright Devourer, the Unspooling Worm — is 'a domain that RESOLVED WRONG and will not resolve back', a hazard with a broken directive and no grievance. ⚑ A TRUE DRAGON IS A PERSON. Older than the Transition, wearing whichever shape the conversation needs, with a want and a name and a story that can be ended badly. ⚠️ Killing one is a tragedy, which is exactly what the bestiary says makes it an NPC. ⛔ AND THE POLYMORPH IS NOT A DISGUISE: `plain_seeming` and `walking_figure` are authored crafts, and a dragon in a human shape is STILL THE DRAGON — it is the same being choosing a smaller door.
_trueDragon: ⚑ NOT A `great_manifestation`. A person, and the bestiary's law is the test: this one has a NAME, a WANT, and a story that can be ended badly.
_vocationWhy: ⛔ `vocation` IS AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED, and the attempt to derive it is the reason. ⚠️ MEASURED 2026-09-08: clustering 40 authored people by their crafts' verb families put SEVENTEEN OF FORTY in KEEPER and ZERO in EDGE — with KESTRIN, THE COLISEUM'S HARM CHAMPION, IN THE KEEPER COLUMN. ⛑ Rank-weighting did not fix it: she reads KEEPER 24 / READER 23 / EDGE 21, essentially flat. ⚑ THE CAUSE IS CLEAN: every capable person carries defensive and perceptive crafts, so verb counts measure COMPETENCE, not PURPOSE. ⛔ A VOCATION IS WHAT A PERSON IS FOR, and that is a judgement — the same shape as `tier`, which a regex also cannot mint. ⬜ `docs/VOCATIONS.md` holds the eight and what each does when a fight starts. ⚑ HERE: ⛑ 'she has been at your table and you did not know.' ⚠️ READER second.
